newsitem.title: UAE: Iran protesters, police clash at Germany's embassy.
newsitem.headline: Iran protesters, police clash at Germany's embassy.

text.p: Several hundred Islamist students clashed on Monday with police at the German embassy in Tehran during a demonstration against a German court's ruling that Iran ordered killings of dissidents in Berlin, witnesses said.
They said the demonstrators charged lines of riot police guarding the embassy in an apparent effort to occupy the compound but were pushed back.

Police, standing six rows deep around the barricaded embassy in central Tehran, stopped several charges by the students who chanted "Death to Germany" and the Moslem rallying cry "Allahu Akbar" (God is Greatest).
Leaders of the protest appealed for calm through loundspeakers to hold back the demonstrators, some of whom threw stones, the witnesses said.
The angry students dispersed after the clashes which lasted less than half an hour.

It was the third demonstration held at the embassy since Friday, a day after a Berlin court sentenced to jail three Lebanese and an Iranian for the 1992 killing of four Iranian Kurdish dissidents in Berlin. The court said senior Iranian leaders had ordered the killings.
Iran has repeatedly denied any role in the killings which it blames on infighting between opposition groups.
Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani has condemned the verdict as provoked by Israel and the United States, but added that a diplomatic row over the ruling was a "passing storm".
Chanting crowds marched in towns and cities across Iran on Monday to protest against the ruling, state-run Tehran radio said.
It broadcast reports from the demonstrations held in a dozen towns and cities ranging from Iran's Caspian coast in the north to the centre and West of the country and stretching to the Gulf coast.

In Tehran, large numbers of bazaar traders held a protest meeting at a mosque and condemned the court's accusations as "yet another plot serving the goals of Arrogance (West) against the Islamic Republic's system of government", it said.
Iran's news agency IRNA said a large number of veterans disabled by Iraqi chemical attacks in the 1980-88 war between the two neighbours would march on Wednesday to the embassy.
The war veterans would also protest against German firms which provided toxic chemicals to Iraq, IRNA said.
Iran has said court proceedings would begin shortly against 24 German companies accused of having helped Iraq produce chemical weapons during its war with Iran.
Iran has responded to the withdrawal of all European Union ambassadors except Greece's by announcing it would pull its envoys out of those countries in return.
Germany made clear at the weekend it would seek to avoid stepping up the dispute with Iran over the ruling.

Bonn officials say privately that, behind the scenes, Iran has signalled it does not wish to raise the temperature in the diplomatic stand-off with a country which, until recently, was its biggest trade partner and friend in the West.
